_comment: Hand-kept notes for the Building Encyclopedia (tools/encyclopedia.py): what each building does and which of its features are in the game. The game never reads this file. The numbers on the page (cost, workers, shelves, levels) come from data/*.json by themselves; only write here what the data can't say. status: built = in the game and settled; trial = in the game, may still change or be undone; planned = decided, not built yet; idea = not decided. Update it when a feature is built (plan.md is the full record). Building ids are the keys at the top; game systems (population, happiness, ...) go under "systems", in the order the page shows them (their numbers come from game_config.json via SYSTEM_FACTS in encyclopedia.py).

population.name: Population
population.summary: The people of your island. Adults work in your buildings and have babies; children grow up into new workers. Newcomers arrive when you have jobs nobody here can fill. People live in households, in the best home they can afford, and pay you rent.

features.text: A new game starts with 50 founding adults living in 5 Public Housing blocks.
People are counted in groups (adults and children), not one by one, so it stays fast on phones.
Births: babies per hour = adults × the birth rate × the birth speed from happiness. A baby needs a free child place (2 per household, house or hut).
Children grow up into adults (new workers) after a few hours.
Deaths: a small share of people each hour (an average life of about 8 real days). The jobless go first, so workers keep their posts.
Migrant workers: a group of up to 5 adults arrives every 2 minutes, but only while a job is open that nobody here can take, and only at 50% happiness or more.
Newcomers don't need a free home: they put up Makeshift Huts by themselves, which go away once they get a real home.
Households of up to 2 adults + 2 children, with a wealth class from their wage (Broke, Poor, Well off, Rich, Filthy rich).
Housing types: Public Housing (free), Regular House and Villa. Each household takes the best home it can afford; with no room, a hut.
Rent: you are the landlord. Rent comes in every hour, also while you're away.
People leave an unhappy island, in groups of 5, the homeless first.
Jobs: whole workers, tied to their building. The emptiest building gets free workers first; warehouses are staffed first.
Wages are paid only for work. Cash can go below zero (debt): nothing can be built until it's paid back.
Wage bonus (None / Small / Good / Big) makes a batch produce 10–30% more units.
Everything keeps happening while you're away, worked out exactly. Welcome back lists who moved in, was born, grew up, died or left.
Statistics → People: groups, children by age, comings and goings, households by wealth, and graphs.
Schools (§5.7): children become graduates, unlocking High-skilled ($30/h) and Professional ($60/h) workers, and with them the Rich and Filthy rich.
More housing types: apartments, condos.
Elderly people and pensions (old age).
A Clinic / healthcare that lowers the death rate.
Events: a festival or an immigration campaign the player pays for, or a boat of newcomers at the Dock.
Tap a house to see made-up named residents ("Maria, 34, Bakery worker"), never saved.
Tune the numbers by playing (birth and death rates, growing-up time, migrant pace).

happiness.name: Happiness
happiness.summary: One % for the whole village, made from three needs: Food, Jobs and Housing. It doesn't make anyone work slower; it decides how fast babies are born, whether job seekers come, and whether people leave the island.

features.text: One village happiness % on the top bar, with a green / gold / red bar. Tapping it opens the breakdown in Statistics → People.
Food need: how many different foods are selling at a Supermarket with workers. More variety = happier (the scale changed on 2026-10-05 when more foods arrived).
Jobs need: the share of adults with a job.
Housing need: the share of households living in a real home, not a hut.
Homeless penalty: every household in a Makeshift Hut takes extra points off, up to a limit.
A small village doesn't complain: needs only count from 10 people.
Grace period: needs don't count in a new village's first 3 hours, so you have time to build jobs and a Supermarket.
Effects in steps: birth speed, job seekers moving in, and people leaving (see the table above).
People leave in groups of 5, faster when very unhappy (2% or 5% an hour).
Worked out fresh from the village each time (never stored, so it can't drift), and exact while you're away.
Happiness changing how fast people work.
Wage bonuses making workers happier.
More needs, e.g. housing quality.
Tune the numbers by playing (food scale, weights, penalty, the steps).

supermarket.summary: Your shop. People of the village buy the food you put on its shelves, a little every hour, and you are paid when a shelf sells out. It is the only way to turn food into money in the village (the Trading Post buys anything, but cheaply).

features.text: The player builds it from the Build menu, Shops tab (it isn't there at the start).
4 shelves; each shelf sells one product, and all shelves sell at the same time.
"Put on a shelf": pick the food, the amount (slider or All) and a price tag. A preview shows the price, how many sell per hour, the time to sell out, sales, cost to make, sales tax and profit.
Five price tags, from Big Sale (−20%, sells 1.95× as fast) to Luxury (+20%, 0.58×).
Village demand: a shelf sells people × the food's appetite × the tag's speed per hour. More people speed up the next shelf you stock.
Variety brings shoppers: +10% for each different product on the shelves beyond the first.
Food only: raw goods like Wheat can't go on a shelf. 34 foods can be sold (Flour, Bread and the Wave 1 foods).
4 fixed workers at the minimum wage, paid only while a shelf is selling. Short of people it sells slower (3 of 4 = 75%).
Paid when a shelf sells out, minus sales tax. Taking a shelf down early (red X) pays for what sold and returns the rest to the Warehouse.
Sells while you're away, exactly; the Welcome back window lists what sold and earned. While playing, a "Sold out" message pops up.
Feeds the village's Food need: the more different foods are selling, the happier people are.
Several Supermarkets: each sells on its own, and stores selling the same food share its shoppers (2 stores = half as fast each).
Upgrades to Level 2, 3 and 4: 5, 6 and 7 shelves. It closes while being upgraded (nothing sells, no wages).
Built with Bricks, Cement, Steel and Construction materials bought at today's market price, plus a construction worker.
Needs a road linked to City Hall, or it gets no workers.
Demolish and Suspend take every shelf down first (paid for what sold). Unsold goods on shelves count in company value.
Its own picture: a Blender design in art Batch B. Until then it shows as a plain box.
Uses electricity (0 MW for now).
Company Tax on shelf sales, once Company Tax is built.
Robotic workers (shown greyed out as "coming soon").
Other store types, each selling its own category (e.g. a Hardware Store for building materials).
Tune the numbers by playing: cost, 4 shelves, 4 workers, appetites, price tags, the +10% variety bonus.
Should fruits share one "fruit" appetite (plan.md §5.17)?
